sections.h2: Who bills and values property in Southfield, Michigan?
sections.html:
The City of Southfield bills and collects its own property tax, and its Treasurer's Office sits in the City Hall Municipal Complex at 26000 Evergreen Road. The counter takes payments from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Southfield is in Oakland County, which takes over any bill the city has not collected by the end of the collection period.

Values come from a separate office. The Assessing Department keeps records of every parcel as of Tax Day, December 31, and sets assessments to 50% of fair market value. It builds those values from property visits, processed transfers of ownership and a two-year sales study, then hears appeals at the March Board of Review.

The split matters when you call. Questions about due dates, payment methods, deferments, special assessments and millage rates go to the Treasurer at (248) 796-5200. Questions about a value, a parcel number, an exemption or a change of mailing address go to Assessing at (248) 796-5230.

sections.h2: When are Southfield summer and winter taxes due?
sections.html:
Summer bills are payable from July 1 through August 31 without penalty, and winter bills from December 1 through February 14. Southfield prints these as payment windows, so the last day of each window is the real deadline.

Southfield payment windows and penalties, from the city Treasurer's Office FAQ and 2026 summer legal notice
BillPay without penaltyFirst penaltyAfter the city period
SummerJuly 1 through August 313.5% added on September 1, then one-half of 1% on October 1 and each month afterOakland County Treasurer adds a 4% collection fee and 1% interest per month
WinterDecember 1 through February 143% added on February 15Payable only to the Oakland County Treasurer after February 28

The 2026 summer notice names March 1, 2027 as the point after which payment goes only to the county. Mailed payments need a USPS postmark no later than the due date, and the city does not accept metered postmarks. Southfield says it cannot extend the deadline for hardship or any other reason, though partial payments are accepted with penalties and interest applying to what remains.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Southfield property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail, online, by phone or in the drop box at City Hall. The fee depends on the route.

  • In person at the Treasurer's counter by check, cash or money order.
  • By mail to City of Southfield Treasurer's Office, 26000 Evergreen Road, Southfield, MI 48076, with the parcel number on the check and the envelope.
  • Online by debit or credit card or electronic check, which carries a 2.3% fee with a $1.95 minimum. Viewing your taxes online is free.
  • By phone at (833) 505-4394, at the same fees as online payment.
  • In the 24-hour drop box to the right of the main entrance on the front circular drive. The box takes no cash.

A bill is not required to pay if you know the amount, but write the parcel ID and a phone number on the check. A mortgage lender that escrows your taxes receives the bill instead of you. If you pay yourself and nothing has arrived by July 1, call the Treasurer for a copy, since a missing bill does not excuse a late payment.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Southfield tax?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax moves from the city to Oakland County after the city collection period, and the cost climbs when it does. The city page says all delinquent taxes and those from earlier years are payable to the Oakland County Treasurer, 1200 N. Telegraph Road, Dept. 479, Pontiac, MI 48341, at (248) 858-0611.

The county adds a 4% collection fee and 1% interest per month until the balance is paid. The city also lists a Delinquent Tax Timeline and an option to pay Oakland County in cash at a 7-Eleven store. An owner who falls behind and wants to sell should get a written payoff from the county before setting a closing date, because the figure changes every month.

sections.h2: What exemptions and relief does Southfield offer?
sections.html:
Southfield lists three exemptions on its Assessing page and a deferment through the Treasurer. Each has its own form and proof requirements.

  • Principal Residence Exemption: owners who claim a house as their principal residence do not pay the school operating mills on the bill.
  • Hardship exemption: residents below Southfield's poverty guidelines may qualify, and the application sits on the Forms page under Assessment Resources.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: a VA disability rating of 100% or more, or a declared unemployable status, may qualify. The claim needs the annual VA Summary of Benefits letter, DD214, VA identification card and driver's license.
  • Summer tax deferment: an owner who lives in the home, has annual income of $40,000 or less, and is 62 or older (or retired because of a disability) may qualify. Applications are accepted only from July 1 through September 15.

The Assessing Department accepts real property transfers and exemption forms by email at contactassessing@cityofsouthfield.com, but every submission needs an original signature. Appointments with staff are booked through the Contact Staff page.

sections.h2: What should I know about Southfield before selling a house here?
sections.html:
Southfield borders Detroit on the south and covers about 26 square miles of land, with Eight Mile Road as its southern edge and Greenfield Road as its eastern edge. The city was incorporated on April 28, 1958, after starting as Southfield Township in 1830, and the Rouge River runs through it. The separate city of Lathrup Village sits as an enclave inside its eastern side.

Offices drive much of the local economy. Wikipedia counts roughly 27 million square feet of office space, second in metro Detroit to downtown Detroit, and the Southfield City Centre area sits near the I-696 and M-10 (Lodge Freeway) interchange. Other main roads are the Southfield Freeway (M-39) and Telegraph Road (US 24). Southfield Public Schools runs a single high school, Southfield A&T, while the northern edge sends students to Birmingham schools and the southeast corner to Oak Park schools.

Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 count 34,860 households in Southfield, with 53.4% living in homes they own. The median value of an owner-occupied unit is $236,200 and the median gross rent is $1,340. A buyer shopping a Southfield house will also compare monthly owner costs, which the Census puts at $1,779 with a mortgage and $764 without one.

sections.h2: How do I handle tax when a Southfield home is sold?
sections.html:
Ask the title company to order a current tax status from the Treasurer before closing and to pay any open balance from the seller's proceeds. Southfield's online property inquiry system shows assessment and tax data for free, but the Treasurer's office should be asked about special assessments such as alarm billing or lawn mowing charges, which may not appear on the latest statement.

Both sides then have paperwork. The Assessing Department takes real property transfers and exemption forms, so ask it which forms the buyer and the seller each owe for your parcel. Change of mailing address requests go to the Assessing Office in writing with the parcel number, a signature and the old and new addresses, and no deed copy is required for a mailing change alone.

A balance does not have to be cleared before listing. Ask the Treasurer for the amount due on the parcel, and have the title company settle it from proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When does Southfield summer tax become late?
faqs.a: Summer tax becomes late after August 31. Southfield adds 3.5% on September 1, then one-half of 1% on the first day of October and each month after that until the balance moves to Oakland County.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Southfield tax bill versus my home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer's Office at (248) 796-5200 for bills, due dates and deferments. Call the Assessing Department at (248) 796-5230 for values, parcel numbers and exemptions.

faqs.q: Can Southfield give me more time to pay?
faqs.a: No extension is available for hardship or other reasons, because state law governs Michigan cities. Partial payments are taken, with penalties and interest on the rest, and seniors or disabled owners who qualify can apply for a summer deferment from July 1 to September 15.

faqs.q: Where do I pay after Southfield turns my bill over to the county?
faqs.a: Pay the Oakland County Treasurer at 1200 N. Telegraph Road, Dept. 479, Pontiac, MI 48341, or call (248) 858-0611. The county charges a 4% collection fee and 1% interest per month on the balance.

faqs.q: How do I claim the Principal Residence Exemption on a Southfield house?
faqs.a: File the exemption claim with the Southfield Assessing Department and sign it with an original signature. Approved owners do not pay the school operating mills portion of the tax bill.
